inputs.share_count_basis: Average number of shares after dilution, H1 2026 6-K (1,205.5m ordinary shares; basic 1,200.4m). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the EUR 5.0bn FY2025 and ~EUR 1bn Q1 2026 buybacks are the cash mechanism that keeps it flat. Ordinary shares, not ADS: 1 ADS = one-half ordinary share.
inputs.net_debt_note: Sanofi-defined net debt at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 6-K line 838): total debt (IFRS, incl. debt-management derivatives) 21,893 less cash and cash-side derivatives 6,380. Up from 11,008 at 31 Dec 2025 after the Dynavax acquisition, EUR 4.9bn dividend and EUR 1.0bn buyback. EXCLUDES lease liabilities of 1,904 (lease treatment B, see lease_treatment).
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 interest income EUR 331m is NOT stripped: Sanofi is a net-debt company (net debt 15.5bn vs owner FCF ~6.4bn), so there is no net cash pile being added to EV and no double count. Interest income sits in financial result, below the EBITDA the component build starts from.
inputs.sbc_source: 20-F FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement, share-based payment expense EUR 313m (FY2024 278, FY2023 283). No cash taxes on net-share settlement disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis), so the add-back is the full charge.
inputs.fx_note: Flows, statements and every per-share value are EUR per ORDINARY share. The Nasdaq quote is USD per ADS and each ADS represents one-half of one ordinary share (20-F FY2025 cover page and Item 12). fx_rate therefore = EURUSD 1.1206 (Yahoo EURUSD=X, 2026-10-09 21:29Z) / 2 ADS per share = 0.5603 USD-per-ADS per EUR-per-share. Parity check: SAN.PA Euronext close of EUR 71.52 on 2026-10-09 x 1.1206 / 2 ties to the SNY Nasdaq close at inputs.price_as_of to within 0.01%, confirming rate, direction and ADS ratio in one line. The research brief's statement that 1 ADS = 1 share is wrong by a factor of two; a 1:1 bridge would have shown the ADS at a 50% discount to Paris.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in EUR, the flows' currency. 10y Bund ~2.7% + beta 0.8 x ERP 5.5% = cost of equity ~7.1%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.3% (2025-26 EUR bond issues), after tax ~2.5%; debt weight ~15% of EV gives a mechanical WACC of ~6.4%. Rounded UP to 7.5% to charge the single-product concentration (Dupixent ~36% of net sales, US biosimilar entry expected early-to-mid 2030s, IRA negotiation eligibility ~2031) in the discount rate. That is the ONLY place concentration risk is charged; the scenarios carry pipeline/R&D-productivity risk and legacy erosion, not a second concentration haircut. The same 7.5% is used in all three scenarios (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost. Sanofi's net debt excludes lease liabilities (20-F FY2025: 'Net debt does not include lease liabilities', 1,739 at Dec-2025, 1,904 at Jun-2026) and the CSV total_debt is bonds and borrowings only, so lease liabilities are kept OUT of net debt and the full lease payment is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path: FY2025 repayments of lease liabilities 333 (financing, 20-F line 21043) plus ~60 of lease interest (1,739 x ~3.5%) = ~393 = 0.9% of revenue. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (3,437 total less ~290 ROU) so the lease is not charged twice. For the record: last_fcf 6,710 follows the contract identity (reported 7,023 - SBC 313); after the 333 lease principal the FY2025 owner FCF is 6,377 (14.6% of revenue), which is the figure the FY2026 component build should be compared with.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (net income attributable to NCI ~EUR 30-40m/yr, <1% of net income); no adjustment. The one material associate (48.2% of Opella) has its share of profit excluded from EBITDA and its carrying value added in equity_bridge (matching-asset rule).
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF, 10-year explicit horizon FY2026-FY2035, scenario-weighted, per .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md (operating company, non-US filer -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md: currency-matched EUR WACC, dual currency EUR/USD with a 2:1 ADS ratio, lease treatment B, matching-asset rule for the Opella stake). First valuation of this ticker; no memory entry. BASE: FY2025 continuing-operations figures only (Opella deconsolidated from Q2 2025; FY2024-25 revenue, OCF and capex in core_metrics are continuing-only). The EBITDA column (12,022 = IFRS operating income 6,344 + D&A and impairment 5,678) is AFTER the Regeneron Alliance profit share (-4,923) and restructuring (-1,138) and BEFORE the 2,241 intangible impairment, so 27.6% is a cash-like, post-one-off anchor; Business operating income was 12,149 (27.8%). EXCLUDED from any base: the 2,874 Opella disposal gain in FY2025 net income, the ~7bn FY2020 Regeneron-stake gain, the FY2017 Animal Health swap gain, and the FY2019 (3,604) / FY2025 (2,241) impairments. FY2025 owner FCF (6,377 after leases) benefited from ~1.6bn of favourable working-capital/provision/deferred-tax movements that the component build does not carry forward, which is why base FY2026 owner FCF (~6.3bn, 13.2% margin) sits slightly below FY2025 despite +9% revenue. 10-year horizon chosen deliberately: it runs through the expected onset of US Dupixent biosimilar competition (early-to-mid 2030s) so the terminal value is capitalised on a post-cliff margin, not a peak one; terminal cap 15x base (market EV/owner-FCF today ~16x). M&A (9.4bn FY2025, Dynavax Feb-2026) is treated as discretionary and is not in the flows; capex at 7.0-7.5% of revenue includes ~1.7bn/yr of licensing and milestone intangible payments, which is the recurring 'pipeline purchase' cost. Guidance anchor: FY2026 net sales ~+10% CER, ~-1% FX (= ~+9% reported), Business EPS growing slightly faster than sales, H2 slower than H1 (H1 2026 +11.1% reported, BOI margin 28.3% vs 27.0%).

equity_bridge.item: Investments accounted for using the equity method (principally the retained 48.2% stake in Opella / OPAL JV Co), at carrying value
equity_bridge.note: 20-F FY2025 balance sheet, Note D.6. (316 at FY2024, before the Opella loss of control). Associates' share of profit is below EBITDA and excluded from the flows, so the asset enters the bridge at book under the matching-asset rule. Carrying value is conservative against the ~EUR 16bn Opella enterprise value implied by the CD&R transaction; H1 2026 share of associates' profit was EUR 2m.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance-anchored base path (FY2026 ~+9% reported decelerating to 1% by FY2034; simple average of the 10-year base growth_rates is 3.7%). Equity CAGR is NOT usable here: FY2025 equity fell on the EUR 5.0bn buyback and Opella deconsolidation, and FY2022-25 revenue/EPS are a mix of Opella-inclusive (to FY2023) and continuing-only (FY2024-25) bases.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 2.5% vs revenue 3.9% and EPS -8.2%: EPS is distorted by the FY2020 Regeneron gain (EPS 9.76) and the FY2025 Opella gain (EPS 6.37 vs continuing 4.03); revenue 3yr CAGR 0.5% compares an Opella-inclusive FY2022 with a continuing-only FY2025. On a like-for-like continuing basis (NetSalesExOpella FY2023 37,817 -> FY2025 43,626) revenue compounded 7.4%/yr. Owner-FCF 3yr CAGR -6.0% vs reported -5.5%: SBC grew 0.72% of revenue from 0.57%, a minor drag.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF series = reported FCF less SBC (interest income not stripped, net-debt company): FY2020 5,061; FY2021 8,235; FY2022 8,080; FY2023 6,951; FY2024 5,134; FY2025 6,710. FY2024 is depressed by Opella separation costs and elevated capex (3,195); FY2021-22 were peak-conversion years.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +9% = guidance ~+10% CER less ~1% FX. FY2027-30 mid-single-digit: Dupixent from 15.7bn to management's ~25bn 2030 ambition (+9.3bn) plus ALTUVIIIO, Beyfortus, Ayvakit, Heplisav-B, Qfitlia and tolebrutinib, net of ~0.7bn/yr legacy erosion (Lantus, Lovenox, Plavix, Aubagio). FY2031-35 fades to 1% as Dupixent faces US IRA negotiation and biosimilar entry while the pipeline only partly backfills.
base.margin_rationale: FY2025 cash-like EBITDA 27.6% (post Regeneron share, post restructuring). H1 2026 BOI margin +1.3pp y/y; guidance has Business EPS growing slightly faster than sales. Base lets the margin expand ~1.8pp to 29.4% by 2030 on operating leverage, then gives back ~1.2pp through 2035 as Dupixent pricing/competition bites.
base.tax_rationale: ETR on business net income 19.9% (FY2025) is struck on a BOI base that excludes ~1.8bn of largely non-deductible intangible amortization; on the component EBIT (after amortization) the equivalent is ~24%, and cash taxes paid 2022-25 averaged ~2.8bn (above business tax expense). 26% in FY2026 easing to 25% (France 25.8%, US 21%, Pillar 2 floor).
base.capex_da_rationale: FY2025 capex 3,538 = 8.1% incl. 1,680 of intangible (licensing/milestone) acquisitions; H1 2026 run-rate 5.9%. Base 7.5% -> 7.0%. D&A ex-ROU ~7.2% (amortization 1,776 + PP&E depreciation ~1,370) drifting to 6.0% as acquired intangibles run off faster than new ones are added.
base.wc_rationale: Receivables + inventories (~19bn) exceed payables (~7bn): growth consumes cash, so -10% of each year's revenue increase.

scenario_narratives.base: Dupixent keeps compounding toward management's ~EUR 25bn 2030 ambition on label expansion (COPD, BP, CSU, AFRS) while the launch cohort (ALTUVIIIO, Beyfortus, Ayvakit, Heplisav-B, Qfitlia, tolebrutinib) roughly offsets legacy erosion, giving ~+9% in FY2026 fading to mid-single digits by 2030. Operating leverage lifts the cash EBITDA margin ~1.8pp to 29.4% by 2030. From 2031 US IRA eligibility and the approach of biosimilar entry cap growth at 1-2% and give back ~1.2pp of margin by 2035; the terminal value is struck on that post-cliff margin at a 15x cap. Bolt-on M&A continues but is funded outside the modelled flows. New CEO Garijo restores a normal, not exceptional, R&D hit rate.
scenario_narratives.bull: Dupixent exceeds EUR 25bn (COPD and further type-2 indications), key US patents hold into the mid-2030s, and at least two late-stage assets (tolebrutinib/Cenrifki in SPMS, frexalimab in MS, duvakitug in IBD, lunsekimig) become multi-billion franchises so that growth stays at 4-5% through 2031. Vaccines stabilise with Beyfortus and Heplisav-B. Margin reaches 31% as the legacy drag shrinks and the Regeneron share of Dupixent profit is diluted by non-collaboration growth; cash tax eases toward 24% on US mix. Terminal growth 2.0%, cap 16x.
scenario_narratives.bear: The 2025-26 pipeline failures (amlitelimab, itepekimab, riliprubart) prove representative: the pipeline does not backfill. Dupixent growth stalls after 2027 on competition (OX40/TSLP/IL-13 entrants, Amgen patent outcome), US rebate pressure and IRA negotiation from 2031, then declines sharply from 2033 as US biosimilars arrive; legacy erosion and insulin price cuts continue unabated and vaccines keep losing US share. Revenue peaks around 2029 and ends 2035 ~5% below FY2026; EBITDA margin compresses to 22.5% as R&D is held up to rebuild the pipeline. Terminal growth 0.5%, cap 12x. Net debt (15.5bn) is comfortably serviceable so this is an earnings-decline bear, not a solvency one.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: ~36% of sales from one product whose US exclusivity ends inside the horizon, and three late-stage failures inside twelve months that cost the CEO his job make the 'pipeline fails to backfill' path a live one, not a tail. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: Dupixent beyond EUR 25bn, patents holding into the mid-2030s, and at least two new blockbusters from a pipeline that has just underdelivered. Base 50%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Large-cap pharma valued on owner free cash flow from continuing operations (ex-Opella), fully charging SBC, Regeneron's Dupixent profit share, restructuring and the recurring licensing/milestone 'pipeline purchase' capex, at a EUR WACC of 7.5% that carries a concentration premium. The ten-year horizon deliberately runs through the Dupixent patent cliff so the terminal value capitalises a post-cliff, not peak, margin. The 48.2% Opella stake is added at book; lease liabilities are charged as operating cost rather than debt. Values are computed in EUR per ordinary share and bridged to USD per ADS at EURUSD/2.
key_risks_to_valuation: Dupixent concentration (~36% of sales): earlier-than-modelled US biosimilar entry, an adverse Amgen/Immunex IL-4 patent outcome, or IRA price negotiation ahead of 2031 would hit base and bull simultaneously
R&D productivity: a further run of phase-3 failures moves the probability mass toward the bear path; conversely a tolebrutinib or frexalimab success is the main upside trigger
M&A outside the flows: another EUR 9bn+ year of acquisitions (FY2025) funded with debt would raise net debt beyond the 15.5bn anchored here and is not charged in the FCF
EUR/USD: ~half of sales are USD; the fx_rate bridges per-share value to the ADS and must be refreshed with the price (refresh_price.py moves the price, not the rate)
Cash tax calibration: the 25-26% rate on component EBIT reconciles business ETR (19.9%), non-deductible amortization and cash taxes paid; a lower effective rate would add ~EUR 3-4/share
Working-capital normalisation: FY2025 owner FCF carried ~1.6bn of favourable WC/provision/deferred-tax movements that are not projected

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API for SNY (Nasdaq ADS, USD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 39.18-52.68 USD. EURUSD=X and SAN.PA from the same endpoint for the fx bridge and parity check (see inputs.fx_note).
